canonical_statement: For a Type-valued presheaf F on a category C, F is representable if and only if there are an object X and an element x of F(X) such that, for every object Y, sending a morphism f : Y -> X to F(f)(x) is a bijection.
domain_and_universes: C : Type u with Category.{v} C; F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w; the proposition lives in an inferred universe
quantifiers: X Y : C, x : F.obj (Opposite.op X), f : Y ⟶ X
hypotheses: C carries the stated category structure
the universal-element side supplies X and x
for every Y, f ↦ F.map f.op x is bijective
conclusion: The universal-element data exist if and only if F.IsRepresentable.
degenerate_and_boundary_cases: Empty categories and empty-valued presheaves are not silently excluded; the existential criterion handles them. Large-category and universe-lift variants require explicit transports and are not credited at intake.
